visual.title: What cognition adds and what biology forbids
visual.alt: Tolman's three groups of rats plotted as errors against days, with the group switched to reward on day eleven dropping almost at once to the level of the always-rewarded group; Garcia and Koelling's result, in which a compound of taste with light and noise is followed by illness or by shock and the illness attaches to the taste while the shock attaches to the light and noise; four cards giving the rules taste aversion breaks and the adaptive reason for each; a contrast between instinctive drift, where reward continues but instinct wins, and extinction, where the reward stopped; and a list matching each researcher to their phenomenon.
visual.caption: The day-eleven drop is the evidence that the map was already built, and the Garcia crossover is the evidence that the brain is not an all-purpose association machine. Together they are what ended the blank-slate reading of conditioning.
